stories.headline: Alvaro Arbeloa praises Fulham attitude amid social media disruption
stories.summary: Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has challenged everyone in his squad to keep showing him a positive attitude and help get the team back on track.
stories.body:
Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa has challenged everyone in his squad to keep showing him a positive attitude and help get the team back on track amid some of his players taking to social media to show their frustration.

The Cottagers head to Liverpool on Saturday still looking for a first point of the new Premier League season.

The home defeat by Crystal Palace last weekend has put the spotlight firmly back on former Real Madrid interim boss Arbeloa, who took over in the summer following the departure of Marco Silva.

Brazilian winger Kevin, an unused substitute against the Eagles, added a cryptic message on his Instagram story with the caption 'no speak, no hear, no see.'

Alex Iwobi and Emile Smith Rowe have, meanwhile, both cleared their own Instagram posts of football-related content, with some fans interpreting it as growing signs of disharmony within the Fulham camp.

Arbeloa, though, stressed all of the players were working hard to turn things around.

"You can learn more about a group after a defeat than after a win, and I saw them work during the week with a very positive attitude, all of them," the Fulham boss told a news conference.

- The numbers behind Premier League's spending power over Europe

"For sure when you are a player and you are not playing, you can't be happy. It is what I expect from the players that are not playing.

"I want that they should need to show me that they are not happy during the training session. For me, this is the most important thing.

"Obviously, when you are not winning games and you are not helping your team, I think you have more desire to play games and to help their teammates.

"But all of them, they have been working so hard and I have a very, very good group with a very good attitude."

Arbeloa knows all too well the challenge that awaits at Anfield having played 98 times for the Reds and helping them reach the 2007 Champions League final before leaving for Real Madrid.

"We have a massive game this week. We know we need to improve and we have to adjust some parts of our game, but we are focused on the game tomorrow," Arbeloa, who reported no fresh injury problems, said.

"We can score goals against any team in the Premier League, that is the thing we are doing so well, creating so many chances and are aggressive without the ball. When you play against a team like Liverpool, with very good players, you need to control them when you have the ball."

Arbeloa added: "You can see that they [Liverpool] are improving, now controlling the games better. I watched their Champions League game against Atlético Madrid, they did a very good game -- they are so aggressive and press high.

"They are so quick up front and have a top squad. Maybe they can make some changes, but they will still start with top players."

stories.headline: Fantasy playbook: NFL Week 1 Shadow Reports, lineup locks and projected scores
stories.summary: An all-encompassing look at the matchups to exploit or avoid and lineup locks in fantasy, as well as projected scores for all NFL games.
stories.body:
Welcome to The Playbook for Week 1!

This column features score projections, over/unders, win probabilities, and of course, easily digestible fantasy advice for seasonlong leagues and DFS. This guide should help you with all sorts of decision-making, including sit/start, last-minute waiver adds and lineup choices.

Additionally, we have folded our Shadow Reports into the game-by-game breakdowns here. Using our play-by-play data, we're able to identify defensive schemes and where each wide receiver and cornerback lines up on each play. By tracking these WR/CB matchups, including potential shadow situations, we can offer the best fantasy guidance each week.

If you want a more detailed look at some of this data, be sure to check out the weekly Shadow Reports: WR vs. CB Cheat Sheet. You can also take a look at the latest analysis of each team's strength of schedule as it stands at the start of the season.

All of this advice is centered on 12-team PPR leagues with relatively standard scoring and lineup settings (1 QB, 2 RB, 3 WR, 1 Flex, 1 K, 1 D/ST), although I'll often mention "shallow" or "deep" leagues for some starters. The charts show all players who have been projected for at least 6.0 fantasy points this week, as well as all D/STs. "Matchup" is automatically determined using a proprietary metric that factors in raw and volume-adjusted fantasy points allowed to each position by the opposing defense.

DFS values in the charts below (and their relative quality) are provided only for Sunday's main slate, which is why there are no values for any games scheduled on days other than Sunday.

Week 1's DraftKings DFS cheat sheet.-->

(Editor's note: Projections and rankings will align almost perfectly, but sometimes when a projection is close, a player might be ranked slightly higher or lower because of other factors, including upside or risk. This column is subject to updates during the weekend, although at the very minimum, rankings will be updated on the site and projections will always be updated inside the game leading up to kickoff.)

TB-CIN | NO-DET | NYJ-TEN | BAL-IND | ATL-PIT | CHI-CAR

CLE-JAC | BUF-HOU | MIA-LV| GB-MIN| WAS-PHI | ARI-LAC| DAL-NYG | DEN-KC

New England Patriots @ Seattle Seahawks
Projected score: Seahawks 25, Patriots 19

Lineup locks: Rhamondre Stevenson, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, A.J. Brown

Fantasy scoop: Jadarian Price is a starting option in the season opener with Zach Charbonnet (PUP) out for at least the first four games of the season. There's some risk here, as Seattle's backfield touch distribution is an obvious unknown, with George Holani and perhaps Emanuel Wilson potential contributors. Of course, the expectation is that the first-round rookie will lead the backfield that finished second in carries and fifth in rushing TDs last season. Even against a solid Patriots defense, Price is an RB2/flex option.

Over/under: 44.1 (10th highest)

Win probability: Seahawks 68% (8th highest)

San Francisco 49ers @ Los Angeles Rams
Projected score: Rams 29, 49ers 22

Lineup locks: Christian McCaffrey, Kyren Williams, Puka Nacua, Davante Adams

Fantasy scoop: George Kittle is questionable to play in the season opener, but even if he is active, there's a good chance he'll be limited and left on fantasy benches. However, if Kittle is sidelined, Jake Tonges is a viable replacement/streaming/DFS option. During the seven games Kittle was sidelined last season (including the playoffs), Tonges handled a 17.9% target share (6.6 per game) and posted a 34-328-3 receiving line. That works out to 11.8 fantasy PPG, which would have ranked eighth among all tight ends, ahead of the likes of Harold Fannin Jr., Travis Kelce, Tyler Warren and Jake Ferguson.

Over/under: 50.9 (Highest)

Win probability: Rams 76% (4th highest)

-->

Tampa Bay Buccaneers @ Cincinnati Bengals
Projected score: Bengals 26, Buccaneers 23

Lineup locks: Joe Burrow, Chase Brown, Ja'Marr Chase, Emeka Egbuka, Tee Higgins

Fantasy scoop: Bucky Irving was viewed as a fringe RB2 throughout draft season and makes for a borderline starting option here in Week 1. Irving has plenty of competition for touches in Kenneth Gainwell and Sean Tucker, but the latter is not fully healthy and may not play much or at all. That's very notable considering that Tucker handled a large bulk of the team's goal line carries down the stretch last season, whereas Irvin had zero carries inside the opponent's 5-yard line on the season.

Irving will face a Cincinnati defense that was poor against running backs last season but that should be better in that area in 2026 after the additions of Dexter Lawrence, Jonathan Allen and Boye Mafe. View Irving as a fringe top-20 back who is a better RB2 option if Tucker is sidelined.

Over/under: 49.8 (2nd highest)

Win probability: Bengals 60% (11th highest)

New Orleans Saints @ Detroit Lions
Projected score: Lions 27, Saints 18

Lineup locks: Jahmyr Gibbs, Travis Etienne Jr., Amon-Ra St. Brown, Chris Olave, Jameson Williams, Sam LaPorta

Fantasy scoop: With Jordyn Tyson sidelined for at least the first four games of the season, both Devaughn Vele and Juwan Johnson are on the fantasy radar. Last season, Johnson posted career-high marks in targets, catches, yardage and fantasy points (all four were eighth or better among tight ends). His nine top-12 fantasy weeks tied for second most at the position. He's a fringe TE1 this week.

Vele is a less proven commodity, but in five games as a full-timer last season (one of which he left hurt), he averaged a solid 5.6 targets per game. That didn't lead to much fantasy production, but he did post an 8-93-1 in Week 13. He's expected to work opposite Olave and is a flex option in deep leagues.

Over/under: 44.8 (9th highest)

Win probability: Lions 81% (2nd highest)

New York Jets @ Tennessee Titans
Projected score: Jets 20, Titans 19

Lineup locks: Breece Hall, Garrett Wilson

Fantasy scoop: Though he's not quite a lineup lock, Carnell Tate cost you roughly a sixth-round pick during draft season, so he's a good bet to be in most lineups this week. History suggests he may not win you the week, but he's also unlikely to crush you.

Over the past decade, 14 wide receivers were selected in the top 15 of the NFL draft and played in Week 1. That group averaged 11.1 fantasy PPG in its debut and was solid, but unspectacular, with 12 of the 14 reaching 9.0 points but only three reaching 16 points (Ja'Marr Chase, Jaylen Waddle, DeVonta Smith). New York's defense is better, though not overly intimidating, and Tate should see plenty of targets as Cam Ward's new top target. The rookie is a viable WR3 in his first professional game.

Over/under: 39.6 (Lowest)

Win probability: Jets 53% (14th highest)

Baltimore Ravens @ Indianapolis Colts
Projected score: Ravens 25, Colts 22

Lineup locks: Lamar Jackson, Jonathan Taylor, Derrick Henry, Zay Flowers, Tyler Warren

Fantasy scoop: Alec Pierce became one of the league's highest-paid wide receivers during free agency, but he also missed nearly all offseason activities after undergoing surgery on his left ankle. The 2022 second-round pick could eventually emerge as a viable WR2/3 in fantasy, but he's a risky Week 1 start in his first game action since last season. Pierce, who is fresh off a career year and has paced all receivers in YPR, YPT and aDOT both of the last two seasons, is no more than a risky flex and is best left on benches against the Ravens.

Over/under: 47.0 (6th highest)

Win probability: Ravens 63% (9th highest)

Atlanta Falcons @ Pittsburgh Steelers
Projected score: Steelers 24, Falcons 16

Lineup locks: Bijan Robinson, Drake London, Michael Pittman Jr., DK Metcalf, Kyle Pitts Sr.

Fantasy scoop: Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle are expected to operate as a two-headed committee this season, with Dowdle likely taking the lead on early downs and Warren highlighted in passing situations. It's possible neither emerges as a weekly starting option, especially in Mike McCarthy's offense.

Consider: During McCarthy's last eight seasons as a head coach, his RB rooms have posted an average finish of 25th in fantasy points (none better than 13th) and 29th in target share (none better than 20th). Atlanta does not present an overly intimidating matchup, but neither back is a recommended start until we have a better feel for the touch distribution.

Over/under: 40.1 (15th highest)

Win probability: Steelers 75% (6th highest)

Chicago Bears @ Carolina Panthers
Projected score: Bears 23, Panthers 22

Lineup locks: D'Andre Swift, Tetairoa McMillan, Rome Odunze, Luther Burden III, Colston Loveland

Fantasy scoop: Chuba Hubbard is coming off a disappointing 2025 campaign in which he battled injury, lost lead-back duties to Rico Dowdle and ranked 64th among 65 qualified backs in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jonathon Brooks, meanwhile, has 12 touches in two pro seasons due to a pair of torn ACLs, but the 2024 second-round pick is only 23 years old and well positioned for a breakout season.

Hubbard (hamstring) missed a chunk of training camp, which opened the door for Brooks to earn a larger share of the backfield pie, but it's unclear which of the two will lead what is likely to be a two-headed committee. This is a situation best avoided in Week 1.

Over/under: 45.5 (8th highest)

Win probability: Bears 54% (13th highest)

Cleveland Browns @ Jacksonville Jaguars
Projected score: Jaguars 24, Browns 17

Lineup locks: Quinshon Judkins, Parker Washington, Harold Fannin Jr.

Fantasy scoop: The Jaguars' running back room is one of Week 1's most-intriguing fantasy storylines, and that discussion starts with Bhayshul Tuten. The second-year back is the best bet to replace Travis Etienne Jr. as Jacksonville's lead back, but he's inexperienced (83 carries and 14 targets as a rookie) and is likely to defer a chunk of the carries to newcomer Chris Rodriguez Jr. The ex-Commander has been effective as rusher but is a nonfactor as a receiver (seven career targets), which is notable with passing down specialist LeQuint Allen Jr. in doubt for this game.

If Allen sits, expect Tuten to handle additional receiving work, which will help solidify him as a fringe RB2 in the opener. Rodriguez should be on benches until we get more clarity on his role.

Over/under: 40.8 (14th highest)

Win probability: Jaguars 75% (5th highest)

Buffalo Bills @ Houston Texans
Projected score: Texans 25, Bills 24

Lineup locks: Josh Allen, James Cook III, David Montgomery, Nico Collins, DJ Moore

Fantasy scoop: Allen was the top quarterback selected in nearly all 2026 fantasy football drafts, but he'll have his hands full with perhaps the league's best defense in Week 1. Allen faced Houston in both of the last two seasons and struggled to fill the box score. In 2024, he completed only nine of his 30 passing attempts for 131 yards and one TD, somewhat bailing out those who started him with 54 rushing yards (14.6 fantasy points). Last season, Allen threw for 253 yards but didn't score a touchdown, threw two INTs, was sacked eight times and produced only 20 rushing yards (8.1 fantasy points).

The Texans defense didn't allow a single quarterback to reach 21 fantasy points in 2025 and remains elite on paper. Allen is too good to bench, but be prepared for a slow start and avoid him in DFS cash games.

Over/under: 48.3 (4th highest)

Win probability: Texans 53% (15th highest)

Miami Dolphins @ Las Vegas Raiders
Projected score: Raiders 24, Dolphins 18

Lineup locks: Ashton Jeanty, De'Von Achane, Brock Bowers

Fantasy scoop: Jeanty (ankle) is questionable to play in the opener against what projects as one of the league's shakiest defenses. If Jeanty is active, he should be in lineups, barring an unlikely report that he'll be severely limited. If Jeanty is sidelined, the picture is perhaps even clearer: Start rookie RB Mike Washington Jr. The fourth-round pick impressed during the preseason and, while he may be limited as a pass catcher in the pros, he has terrific upside as a rusher, partially due to his combination of size (6-1/223) and speed (4.33 40-yard dash). Washington would figure to operate as Las Vegas' clear feature back, with Dylan Laube as his primary competition.

Over/under: 41.6 (13th highest)

Win probability: Raiders 71% (7th highest)

Green Bay Packers @ Minnesota Vikings
Projected score: Packers 22, Vikings 21

Lineup locks: Justin Jefferson

Fantasy scoop: Josh Jacobs is on the commissioner's exempt list and will not be eligible to play in Week 1. With the Packers' feature back sidelined, MarShawn Lloyd is expected to operate as the lead back, with Chris Brooks and perhaps Pierre Strong Jr. also involved. Lloyd is an unproven commodity (he's appeared in one game in two pro seasons due to a variety of injuries), but the 2024 third-round pick is well positioned for 15 or so touches in Matt LaFleur's RB-friendly scheme. There's obvious risk, especially against a good Minnesota defense, but Lloyd can be viewed as an RB2/flex option in the season opener.

Over/under: 43.7 (11th highest)

Win probability: Packers 54% (12th highest)

Washington Commanders @ Philadelphia Eagles
Projected score: Eagles 28, Commanders 19

Lineup locks: Jalen Hurts, Jayden Daniels, Saquon Barkley, DeVonta Smith, Terry McLaurin

Fantasy scoop: Smith and McLaurin are lineup locks, but that may be where your exposure to wide receivers in this game ends. Stefon Diggs is a possible flex option, but his role is a bit uncertain as he moves from the No. 1 target in New England's high-scoring offense to perhaps the No. 2 target in a lower-volume passing game. He'll also be dealing with a good Eagles defense that allowed six touchdowns to wide receivers all of last season.

As for the Eagles, Makai Lemon was injured for a chunk of offseason activities and very well could be limited in his pro debut. Any Lemon limitation would benefit Dontayvion Wicks, but the uncertainty means you're likely betting on a big play or two if he's in your flex over safer options. Even in a good matchup, both Eagles secondary receivers are best left on benches.

Over/under: 47.9 (5th highest)

Win probability: Eagles 80% (3rd highest)

Arizona Cardinals @ Los Angeles Chargers
Projected score: Chargers 29, Cardinals 17

Lineup locks: Justin Herbert, Omarion Hampton, Jeremiyah Love, Ladd McConkey, Trey McBride

Fantasy scoop: Love is listed as a lineup lock primarily because you're unlikely to sit your second- or third-round pick in Week 1, but keep in mind that, if he's active, he very well could be limited. Love, who suffered an ankle sprain in his preseason debut, is talented enough to do a lot with a little, so he'll still be on the RB2 radar if ready to roll against the Chargers.

Of course, if Love is ruled out, Tyler Allgeier will make for a solid RB2 option. The ex-Falcon has been limited to a situational role throughout most of his career, but he did score eight touchdowns last season and was effective when operating as a lead back during parts of the 2022 and 2023 seasons.

Over/under: 46.3 (7th highest)

Win probability: Chargers 87% (Highest)

Dallas Cowboys @ New York Giants
Projected score: Cowboys 26, Giants 23

Lineup locks: Jaxson Dart, Dak Prescott, Javonte Williams, Cam Skattebo, CeeDee Lamb, Malik Nabers, George Pickens

Fantasy scoop: Nabers (ACL) is trending toward playing in Week 1 and, if he does, he should be in lineups. There's risk that he may be somewhat limited in his first game action since Week 4 of last season, but he'll certainly be on the field when New York is passing and, considering he cost you a second- or third-round pick, it's unlikely that you have a better alternative on your bench. In 18 full games in his career, Nabers has a massive 35% target share (11.3 per game) and he's averaging 18.2 fantasy PPG, so he can afford a short-term dip in usage and still provide starting-caliber numbers in fantasy.

The Dallas defense is expected to be better this season, but cornerback remains a potential weakness, which only helps Nabers' cause in Week 1. Note that, if Nabers is out, the likes of Darnell Mooney and rookie Malachi Fields will be risky flex options.

Over/under: 49.5 (3rd highest)

Win probability: Cowboys 62% (10th highest)

Denver Broncos @ Kansas City Chiefs
Projected score: Chiefs 22, Broncos 21

Lineup locks: Kenneth Walker III, Rashee Rice, Jaylen Waddle, Courtland Sutton

Fantasy scoop: The season's first Monday Night Football game will feature a pair of quarterbacks who perhaps will be left on fantasy benches. Patrick Mahomes is set for his first action since suffering a torn ACL in Week 15 last season, but it's possible his mobility will be severely limited -- and he'll be dealing with one of the league's best pass defenses. Mahomes hasn't cleared 17.3 fantasy points against Denver since Week 17 of 2022, averaging 13.2 PPG during the four-game span. He should be on benches this week.

Bo Nix, meanwhile, was a terrific value in 2026 fantasy drafts, but he'll open the season on the road against a good Chiefs defense that has held him to fantasy point totals of 16.1, 12.6 and 19.5 in three career matchups (Nix scored 33.5 against Chiefs backups in Week 18 of 2024, so that is excluded). That's not terrible production from Nix, of course, so while he deserves a slight downgrade, his dual-threat ability keeps him on the QB1 radar.

Over/under: 43.3 (12th highest)

Win probability: Chiefs 52% (Lowest)

stories.headline: Indiana Pacers offseason recap, early 2026-27 season preview
stories.summary: Will Haliburton's return push the Pacers back to the top of the East? Looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season.
stories.body:
The Indiana Pacers have experienced some of the highest highs and lowest lows the NBA has to offer the last two season and they now enter the 2026-27 season healthy and with a fresh outlook.

Two-time All-Star Tyrese Haliburton returns after a torn Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 Finals kept him out all of last season, and with him come the expectations that the Pacers will be back in the Eastern Conference playoff mix. Indiana missed out on a potential top four pick in June's draft, but still acquired Ivica Zubac at last year's trade deadline to pair with Haliburton.

Pascal Siakam also returns to help the Pacers bounce back from a 19-63 record last season, and the team brought in Kelly Oubre Jr. and Larry Nance Jr. to add depth to an already experienced roster.

Will Haliburton's return in Indianapolis be enough to make the Pacers a contender in the upgraded East?

ESPN's staff of experts is looking back at the offseason and taking an early look at the 2026-27 season for all 30 teams, with 30 pieces -- one for every team -- rolling out each weekday through Sept. 18. We're answering the biggest looming questions, evaluating X factors and much more for all 30 teams.

Quick links:

Roster | Depth chart | Transactions

More Pacers coverage | More NBA

Offseason at a glance
Key additions: Kelly Oubre Jr., Larry Nance Jr.

Key retentions: None

Key subtractions: C Micah Potter

The Pacers didn't make any major offseason changes, but they will have two major additions to the roster they were missing last year: starting center Ivica Zubac, who was acquired at the trade deadline from the Clippers, and star guard Tyrese Haliburton, returning from injury for the first time since the 2025 NBA Finals. Haliburton's presence lifted the Pacers into an Eastern Conference contender in 2024 and '25, and 16 months after a torn Achilles, they'll be counting on him to do the same in 2027. And Zubac will provide a different kind of center than Myles Turner provided the last time Haliburton was on the court. -- Jamal Collier

Zach Kram's offseason grade: B-

The Pacers embarked on their summer activity early, dealing a big package -- which included the eventual No. 5 pick -- for Ivica Zubac at the trade deadline in February.

Since the offseason began, they've focused exclusively on their bench, adding Kelly Oubre Jr. and Larry Nance Jr. on short-term deals. The next potential order of business is extension talks for Tyrese Haliburton and Pascal Siakam, though that's not a pressing concern because both players are still under contract for multiple years. -- Kram

What we learned over the past few months
From Ben Golliver's offseason lessons piece: Indiana has everything it needs for a bungee jump season.

The Pacers deservedly caught some grief over the finer points of their midseason trade for center Ivica Zubac, which wound up costing them the No. 5 pick in June's draft. Kevin Pritchard, Indiana's president, won't hear the end of it if Keaton Wagler blossoms into a star for the LA Clippers.

Nevertheless, Zubac is a clear upgrade over Myles Turner, Indiana's starting center during its surprising run to the 2025 Finals. After plummeting from 50 wins in 2024-25 to a 19-win gap season while franchise guard Tyrese Haliburton recovered from an Achilles injury, the Pacers are poised to bounce right back up the standings.

Finding a capable center was Indiana's top priority during Haliburton's absence, and Zubac outperformed Turner last season in scoring, rebounding, player efficiency rating and win shares. Otherwise, the Pacers bring back plenty of familiar faces from their Finals run, including Pascal Siakam, Aaron Nesmith, Andrew Nembhard, T.J. McConnell and Obi Toppin. Veteran coach Rick Carlisle hasn't gone anywhere, either.

Pessimists will argue that the Pacers caught lightning in a bottle two years ago, and that replicating their magical late-season run is too much to ask. Maybe so, but Haliburton's unique ability to get the most out of his teammates should restore Indiana to respectability. -- Golliver

The big question: How will the bench hold up?
Aside from Haliburton's brilliance and late game heroics, one the strengths for the Pacers during their NBA Finals run two seasons ago was the depth of their bench. Some of that depth has dwindled in the past year. Bennedict Mathurin has moved on, T.J. McConnell declined a bit last season without Haliburton and the Pacers haven't found another key reserve to pick up the slack. Rick Carlisle has been one of the best coaches in the league at pushing the right buttons with his rotation, and especially if the team plans to ease Haliburton back from injury at all, they will need to lean on their depth to get through the regular season. -- Collier

Basketball Power Index rank: No. 15
Here are the predicted Net Points per 100 possessions for the Pacers' top seven players for the 2026-27 season:

Haliburton was taken No. 12 in the 2020 draft and was quickly traded from his original team, but is arguably the best player from that Draft, ahead of No. 1 pick Anthony Edwards. He doesn't score as much and has been named only All-NBA Third Team compared to Edwards' Second Teams, but Haliburton has posted better performance across most player metrics: EPM, LEBRON, xRAPM, Net Points (not DARKO). -- Dean Oliver

Read about how Net Points works here.

Biggest injury returns for the 2026-27 NBA season

Biggest X factor
Ivica Zubac

Essentially the entire Pacers rotation that reached the 2024-25 Finals will return next season, with Haliburton back -- but with one key exception. Myles Turner fit into Indiana's system because of his shot-blocking prowess and 3-point spacing, but Zubac is a superior center overall. At his best, Zubac has been an All-Defensive honoree and All-NBA candidate.

He wasn't at his best last season, however, and now he's 29 years old, recovering from a broken rib and adjusting to a drastically different system than he's ever played in before. (He played just five games for the Haliburton-less Pacers after last season's trade.) Zubac might offer a lower floor than Turner, just because of his uncertain fit with the up-tempo Pacers. But his ceiling is much higher. -- Kram

Fantasy insight from our expert
Fantasy insight ahead of the season: The Pacers finished 12th in the NBA in assists last season (27.7 APG) with point guard Tyrese Haliburton sidelined, but they had finished third (29.2 APG) and first (30.8 APG) in the two seasons prior. With Haliburton back and running Coach Rick Carlisle's motion offense, the Pacers should again return to the top of the league in the category. And team assists lead to team points, which is good for the fantasy prospects of all Pacers rotation players.-- Andre Snellings

stories.headline: Fantasy baseball news and notes: Carroll ready for playoff push and more for Friday

stories.body:
Everything that happens in and around MLB has some additional context when viewed from a fantasy baseball perspective. From lineup changes to minor league call-ups to injuries and so much more, the news cycle will constantly affect player values in fantasy baseball.

Our fantasy baseball buzz file, with contributions from our ESPN fantasy writers, aims to provide fantasy managers with the intel they need as news breaks around MLB.

Key links: RP depth chart | Player Rater | Scoring leaders

10-day pitching forecaster | 10-day hitting forecaster

Sept. 11: Friday's news to know
By Todd Zola

After a light Thursday, everyone is in action today, with the Chicago Cubs and Pittsburgh Pirates kicking things off at 2:20 p.m. ET with a Wrigley Field matinee.

Corbin Carroll is expected to return to the Arizona Diamondbacks tonight. He missed the club's last two games due to a sore lower back. He went for an MRI on yesterday's off day, and it came back negative. Carroll's return is timely, with the Diamondbacks opening a series with the Texas Rangers only one-half game behind the San Diego Padres for the last NL wild-card spot.
Brandon Marsh exited Thursday afternoon's game after fouling a ball off his foot in the eighth inning. The Philadelphia Phillies open an important road series with the Atlanta Braves tonight and Marsh's status is uncertain. The Phillies are four games behind the Braves for the NL East lead.
The Washington Nationals placed Nasim Nunez on the bereavement list. He's expected to miss this weekend's home set with the Los Angeles Angels. Nunez leads the majors with 46 stolen bases.
The St. Louis Cardinals are optimistic that Masyn Winn will return to the lineup tonight when they entertain the Chicago White Sox. The slick-fielding shortstop was activated from the IL on Tuesday after recovering from a broken left thumb, but he was unable to play Wednesday because of residual soreness. After yesterday's off day, Winn is now expected to be ready to take the field.

Be sure to check out the latest fantasy lineup advice as well as the MLB betting tips for Friday.

Sept. 10: Thursday's news to know

By Todd Zola

It's a light day in MLB, with only five games on the schedule. The Atlanta Braves and Tampa Bay Rays get things started at Truist Field at 12:15 p.m. ET. Two more afternoon games follow, then two night games.

Shohei Ohtani missed his second straight game last night and he's appeared only once in the Los Angeles Dodgers' last seven contests. The two-way star is nursing a sore knee and biceps. The club had hesitated to place him on the 15-day IL, but finally relented last night.
To replace Ohtani, the Dodgers are calling up Josue De Paula from Double-A Tulsa, who will join the team for Friday's matchup with the Miami Marlins. De Paula is No. 10 overall in Kiley McDaniel's updated 2026 MLB top 100 prospect rankings. The 21-year-old outfielder hit .303/.401/.547 with 27 homers and 31 steals in 124 games for the Drillers.
The New York Yankees will be without 2B Jazz Chisholm Jr. for at least 10 days and possibly the rest of the regular season after placing him on the 10-day IL. He sprained his right thumb sliding into second base Tuesday night. The club will reportedly recall Anthony Volpe from Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. Along with Jose Caballero, Volpe is an option to fill in at second.
Hagen Smith is set to make his first MLB start tonight when the Chicago White Sox entertain the Pittsburgh Pirates. He is ranked No. 4 in McDaniel's updated prospect rankings. The 23-year-old left-hander has made 10 big league appearances out of the bullpen, posting a pristine 0.56 ERA and an 0.94 WHIP over 16 innings. He's averaged 34 pitches over his last four outings, so Smith won't likely pitch deep into the game.

stories.headline: What makes Max Verstappen so good? Career, background and F1 records
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is facing 100 drivers in a unique event called Max vs. 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 challengers, starting from the back of the grid.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and is taking part in a unique event called Max vs 100 where the Formula 1 star will attempt to overtake 100 drivers, starting from the back of the grid.

The 28-year-old currently races in F1, the highest tier in motorsport. He is one of the fiercest competitors out there and is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking.

But if you have never heard of him, or want to learn more, here is everything you need to know.

- Max vs 100: F1 superstar Verstappen to race drivers in karting event - live on Disney+

Who is Max Verstappen?
Verstappen was born in Belgium to his Dutch father Jos and his Belgian mother Sophie. His father raced in F1 between 1994-2003 and had two podium finishes, while his mother competed in karts. He currently resides in Monaco.

Who does he race for?
Verstappen started racing go-karts when he was just four years old and started to compete in championships at seven.

He then made his way through the ranks winning several world and European titles in 2013. He raced just one season in Formula 3 before skipping Formula 2 and heading straight to Formula 1.

In 2015, he signed for Red Bull junior team Toro Rosso at the age of 17 before he was promoted to Red Bull a year later.

He then went on to become the youngest ever grand prix winner after taking victory at the Spanish Grand Prix and has been at Red Bull ever since, becoming the most successful driver at the team.

He signed a long-term contract back in March 2022 to stay at the Milton Keynes-based team until the end of 2028, and before the Dutch Grand Prix this year he penned a new deal keeping him at the team until 2030.

What has he achieved?
It was clear from the early days that Verstappen was going to be an exceptional racing driver and he's become a phenomenon since with a killer instinct.

He's had 244 race starts in F1 and has been on the top step of the podium 71 times. He's been on the podium 131 times and is just two pole positions away from reaching 50 career poles.

The Dutchman has four world championships which he won back-to-back in a dominant Red Bull era between 2021-2024.

He also has an impressive list of achievements to his name, one being in 2023 where he recorded the most wins [19] and the most podium finishes [21] in a single season. He also recorded 10 consecutive race victories.

When is Max vs 100?
The event is taking place on Sept. 16 and will be streamed live on Disney+.

Why is he racing in Max vs 100?

Verstappen has never been shy of getting his teeth stuck into other forms of motorsport away from Formula 1. He most recently made his debut at the iconic Nürburgring 24 Hours in May, driving a Mercedes-AMG GT3.

This will be a slightly different challenge for the Dutchman, but no doubt one he will enjoy with his competitive nature.

"In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking," Verstappen said. "Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it's always nice to return."

The event is taking place at Silverstone in the U.K. and a circuit has been purpose-built for the occasion. It's set to be the biggest go-kart event in the world.

- Max Verstappen deal: Good news for Red Bull and F1, bad news for the driver market

- Max Verstappen ends F1 speculation by signing new Red Bull contract to 2030

How is his 2026 F1 season going?
The 2026 season is one with big regulation and rules changes and Red Bull are currently at the back of the front running teams, but are ahead of the midfield pack.

Verstappen is still searching for his first race win of the season, but has been on the podium four times.

He's currently sixth in the title championship and is 130 points adrift from title leader Kimi Antonelli.

stories.headline: Kings' Kevin Fiala has further surgery, to miss start of camp
stories.summary: Kings forward Kevin Fiala will miss the start of training camp after undergoing follow-up surgery for the broken leg he sustained during the Milan Cortina Olympics.
stories.body:
LOS ANGELES -- Kings forward Kevin Fiala will miss the start of training camp after undergoing follow-up surgery for the broken leg he sustained during the Milan Cortina Olympics.

Fiala missed the second half of the NHL season and the playoffs after he was hurt playing for Switzerland in a preliminary round game on Feb. 13. He broke his left femur in a collision with Canada forward Tom Wilson and had to be stretchered off the ice. He had surgery in Italy.

Fiala had 18 goals and 22 assists in 56 games for the Kings last season. The 30-year-old winger has been one of Los Angeles' top offensive contributors since being acquired in a trade from the Minnesota Wild in June 2022 as a restricted free agent. The Kings then signed him to a seven-year contract.

The Kings did not announce a timeline for Fiala's recovery. Los Angeles plays its season opener at the Colorado Avalanche on Sept. 30, a rematch of the four-game sweep that marked the Kings' fifth straight first-round exit.

stories.headline: Team USA scores 108 in rout of Hungary to reach FIBA semis
stories.summary: The U.S. routed Hungary 108-56 to advance to the semifinals of the women's FIBA World Cup and stretched its winning streak in the tournament to 34 games.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- After a scare in the group phase against Italy, Team USA knew it wouldn't be able to play poorly in the knockout rounds of the FIBA World Cup if it wanted to come away with a fifth straight gold medal and 12th overall.

It was only the quarterfinals, but the U.S. responded to that challenge, putting together what the team viewed as its best performance of the tournament with a 108-56 drilling of Hungary. The Americans' 108 points and 31 assists were both records for a World Cup quarterfinal game.

Napheesa Collier led all scorers with 19 points -- a personal best with the senior national team -- followed by 15 from Rhyne Howard and 10 each from Kahleah Copper, Caitlin Clark and Jackie Young.

"We talked about just getting better with each game, and I think we did that today, especially with how we shared [the ball]," Howard said. "I think if we continue to play like that and continue to keep everybody on the same page, continue to move the ball, it's going to be really hard to stop us."

Added Collier: "We were moving the ball a lot. It wasn't one-on-one. We were looking for a great shot, not just a good shot, and so when we play that way, it's really fun. And I feel like our chemistry is building each game."

The U.S. will face either Spain or Australia in Saturday's semifinal, which will tip at 2 p.m. ET.

The Americans got out to a hot start, jumping ahead 36-12 at the end of the first quarter and leading 59-30 at the half. Their defense frustrated Hungary, which saw star post duo Dorka Juhasz and Virag Takacs-Kiss combine for just four points.

The U.S. had 25 of its 44 points off turnovers at the half, using defense to fuel offense on the other end.

"Everybody's just all dialed in offensively and defensively," said Angel Reese, who finished with nine points, six rebounds and three assists. "We talked about our keys, what it's going to take to win gold, and I think tonight we did everything that coach asked us to do."

Two games after Italy held the U.S. to 55 points, the Americans got mostly whatever they wanted offensively. Their 58.8% field goal percentage was their best clip of the tournament, and 12 3-pointers matched their tournament high after shooting 29% from deep in the group stage.

Team USA also won the inside battle Thursday, its 32 paint points at the half (52 overall) were more than the entire Hungary team had scored at that point.

"I feel like today was a really good one for us," Collier said. "We worked on some defensive schemes that we wanted to get better at, some offensive stuff that we wanted to clean up, and so I feel like we went out and executed that."

The 108 points marked the second most scored in a knockout game in World Cup history, behind only Brazil's 110 against the U.S. in the 1994 semifinals. The 52-point win margin was the second largest for a quarterfinal in World Cup history.

"I thought it started with our activity on the defensive end," coach Kara Lawson said. "And so our ability to turn them over, get out in transition, get some advantage plays, 2-on-1, 3-on-2, I thought gave us a lot of confidence early. And then our ability to shoot the 3-point shot ... we have a really good 3-point shooting team, and so I just thought that's what kind of jump-started us."

Lawson and the players agreed the performance was a product of their expedited chemistry-building finally starting to come into fruition. Unlike many national teams, the U.S. did not have a training camp or much prep time together before arriving in Berlin, last gathering as a group (and not its final roster) at the Final Four in April. They have now been together for about 10 days after leaving their WNBA teams.

"The more we play, the more comfortable we're getting with each other," said Young, the only American to hit double figures in each game this tournament. "And tonight we got the ball popping and we were able to get some easy buckets in transition."

Added Collier: "Today felt good, not just because of the score, but in the way that we were scoring as well."

stories.headline: No Ferrari, but Shark is as reliable as they come
stories.summary: After undergoing 15 surgeries during his NRL career, Cameron McInnes revels in the process of recovery and not feeling the best.
stories.body:
Cameron McInnes has made a career out of not feeling comfortable on a rugby league field.

As Cronulla teammate Addin Fonua-Blake put it recently, for more than a decade "that guy has put his face, and not just his body, on the line every week".

By McInnes' own count he has undergone "14 or 15 surgeries" throughout his 243-game NRL career, covering almost every body part with the exception of his shoulders.

All of which, the departing Sharks lock has somewhat enjoyed.

Not because he likes injuries, but the routine and challenge of recovering from them plays right into his hands.

"Some players have to feel like a Ferrari, whereas that's not me," McInnes quips.

"I'm not a car man, but I guess I'm some beaten down thing that does the job.

"I've just learnt to never feel that good out there."

For this entire year, McInnes' approach has had him treating every NRL game as if it may be his last.

It sounds cliche, but last year's surprise diagnosis of an ACL rupture after playing through the pain and later mowing the lawn has taught McInnes to think that way.

This month though, McInnes does know for sure one game will be his last in the NRL, beginning with Saturday night's clash against North Queensland.

Bound for York in the English Super League, McInnes has one month to win a maiden premiership.

"It's really hard, because most footy players are the same. They're so focused on looking to the next thing," McInnes said.

"And because the next week is such a massive opportunity for the club, not just me, for the club, it's still really hard to reflect on (my career) right now.

"I'm not that emotional or sentimental anyway."

For many, the tough-as-nails McInnes is a throwback to another age of rugby league, where beaten up cars were valued in the same way as Ferraris.

But the South Sydney junior is quick to point out that the faster game in fact helped his career, facilitating a move from hooker to a mobile ball-playing lock.

It was in that role he won a NSW State of Origin jersey in 2024, after narrowly missing out as a dummy-half at St George Illawarra in 2018.

McInnes is adamant players like him will always be needed, if not universally recognised.

"The way that the game's covered now, which is great entertainment, it's all about line breaks, tries, those flashy moments," McInnes said.

"Whereas that's probably not been the basis of my game.

"If you ask any coach in the NRL they still value that, but it's just more what the media have to highlight.

"You look at guys that are being talked about and sometimes it's like, oh yeah, it's probably because of those moments they have in games.

"But games go for 80 minutes, not 30 seconds."

stories.headline: NFL Week 1 picks, predictions, schedule, odds, fantasy tips
stories.summary: Josh Allen vs. C.J. Stroud? Jayden Daniels vs. Jalen Hurts? There are 14 games left in Week 1, and we have picks, predictions, key stats, watchability ratings and more.
stories.byline: NFL Nation, Pamela Maldonado, Eric Moody, Ben Solak and Seth Walder
stories.body:
Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season is here! The first kickoff weekend is full of intriguing quarterback showdowns and new team debuts for Jared Verse, Tua Tagovailoa, David Montgomery, Kyler Murray and Kirk Cousins, among others. We have Josh Allen vs. C.J. Stroud. We have Derrick Henry vs. Jonathan Taylor. And we have Packers vs. Vikings and Cowboys vs. Giants.

We're here to get you ready for the action. First, our NFL Nation reporters take you inside the locker room with the best thing they heard this week, and ESPN Research provides a key stat to know. Then, analytics writer Seth Walder makes a bold prediction for each matchup, NFL analyst Ben Solak gives one reason to tune into each game (and rates the watchability of the matchup), fantasy analyst Eric Moody shares fantasy football intel and betting analyst Pam Maldonado provides betting insight. We also have Football Power Index (FPI) game projections, and Maldonado, Moody and Walder all give us final score picks for every game.

Let's get into the full Week 1 slate, which culminates with "Monday Night Football" matchup between Denver and Kansas City on ESPN. (Game times are Sunday unless noted, and all odds are via Draftkings.)

Jump to a matchup:

BUF-HOU | BAL-IND | TB-CIN

NO-DET | CHI-CAR | ATL-PIT

CLE-JAX | NYJ-TEN | GB-MIN

WSH-PHI | ARI-LAC | MIA-LV

DAL-NYG | DEN-KC

Previously played:

NE-SEA | SF-LAR

What ESPN Analytics says ...

Bills at Texans
1 p.m. ET | CBS | BUF -1.5 (44.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Bills: Buffalo's reimagined defense has an idea of what to expect from the Texans' offense. "We expect multiple different personnel groupings and for them to try and run the ball," edge Bradley Chubb said. "You look at their offseason additions, they let it be known what they want their offense to be." He's talking about the Texans signing RB David Montgomery and TE Foster Moreau and selecting a guard and a tight end in the first two rounds of the draft. What Buffalo's defense will look like under first-time coordinator Jim Leonhard is one of the key early storylines in the AFC. -- Dan Graziano

What we're hearing on the Texans: Safety Jalen Pitre said Houston has to "keep [Bills quarterback Josh Allen] from playing backyard football." But in reality, Allen playing backyard football plays right into Houston's advantage. In the past two matchups against Allen, he is 13-of-34 for 201 passing yards with two interceptions and nine sacks when he holds the ball for longer than 2.5 seconds, according to NFL Next Gen Stats. -- DJ Bien-Aime

Stat to know: The Texans' five-game home win streak is tied with the Rams and Seahawks for the longest active streak in the NFL. A win would tie their longest home win streak in franchise history, including the playoffs. -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Bills WR DJ Moore will be held to two or fewer receptions. Perhaps Buffalo's newest playmaker will deliver at some point this season. But I don't think it will be against Derek Stingley Jr. or Kamari Lassiter. -- Walder

Viewers rating (out of 10): 8.8. The Texans and Bills played a great game in primetime last season -- the Texans were victorious on the back of a passionate defensive outing as backup quarterback Davis Mills did just enough to win 23-19. I bet we see a vengeful Allen (eight sacks, two picks) this time. -- Solak

Injuries: Bills | Texans

Fantasy nugget: Allen finished with just 8.1 fantasy points in their meeting last season. Houston also gave up the third-fewest fantasy points per game to QBs in 2025. See Week 1 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: Texans unders are 33-18 under DeMeco Ryans, the second-highest rate since 2023 (Chiefs, 34-17). The Texans can pressure Allen and keep numbers in coverage, and Buffalo also consistently started slow despite its offensive abilities. The matchup points toward longer drives and fewer possessions. Read more. -- Maldonaldo

Maldonado's pick: Texans 20, Bills 17

Moody's pick: Texans 23, Bills 20

Walder's pick: Bills 24, Texans 17

FPI prediction: BUF, 54.5% (by an average of 1 point)

Matchup must-reads: Big energy, big reward? Brady is full of caffeine and confidence ... Texans' Stroud confident ahead of the biggest season of his life

Ravens at Colts
1 p.m. ET | CBS | BAL -3.5 (47.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Ravens: This is QB Lamar Jackson's first game with new OC Declan Doyle, but the two-time NFL MVP is familiar with Colts DC Lou Anarumo, who was the longtime coordinator with the Bengals. Jackson has excelled in his past four games against Anarumo's defenses, throwing 10 touchdowns and two interceptions, while averaging 258.5 passing yards. "He does a pretty good job of being able to keep you off-balance and attack you," Doyle said of Anarumo. "It's very similar to how we try to attack defenses." -- Jamison Hensley

What we're hearing on the Colts: Indianapolis enters with significant personnel changes on defense and at least five new starters. How it all comes together, against a Baltimore offense with prolific potential, is anyone's guess. "Anybody would be curious on how everything's going to shake out," said DT DeForest Buckner, who returns after season-ending neck surgery in 2025. "But all that matters is the trust that you build ... and the chemistry that you build on the field." -- Stephen Holder

Stat to know: The Ravens averaged 24.9 points (11th in the NFL) and 333.2 yards (16th) in 2025 -- their fewest YPG in any season since 2017. -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Colts RB Jonathan Taylor will record four or more receptions. Last season, no team ran more zone coverage than the Chargers under then-defensive coordinator Jesse Minter. Now, he's coaching the Ravens. And RBs record receptions against zone at a much higher rate than against man. -- Walder

Viewers rating (out of 10): 8.6. There's a lot of intrigue in this one. What does the Minter/Doyle braintrust look like in Baltimore? Just how healthy are QB Daniel Jones and WR Alec Pierce? And there should be plenty of points. -- Solak

Injuries: Ravens | Colts

Fantasy nugget: Zay Flowers is dangerous from both the slot and the outside, and the Colts gave up the sixth-most fantasy points per game to WRs last season. Doyle is incorporating more under-center formations and play-action to maximize Jackson and Flowers, which could lead to more chunk plays. See Week 1 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: The Colts are 3-14-1 ATS (against the spread) in Week 1 since 2008. The Colts' defense was already one of the league's worst at preventing opponents from moving the ball, and now it has to deal with Jackson, plus an upgraded pass rush on the other side with edge Trey Hendrickson. Indianapolis has offensive upside, but Jones is returning from an Achilles injury. Read more. -- Maldonaldo

Maldonado's pick: Ravens 27, Colts 21

Moody's pick: Ravens 30, Colts 20

Walder's pick: Ravens 21, Colts 14

FPI prediction: BAL, 59.8% (by an average of 2.4 points)

Matchup must-reads: How Ravens' Henry is driven to rank among NFL's best backs ... Colts' Pierce (ankle) expected to play in Week 1 ... QB Jones has one box left to check in dramatic return

Buccaneers at Bengals
1 p.m. ET | Fox | CIN -3.5 (50.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Buccaneers: Coach Todd Bowles called playing QB Joe Burrow a "cat and mouse game" because he is so good at recognizing coverages. "He is outstanding at seeing what you're in." All the more reason they're hoping their remade pass rush -- with first-round draft pick Rueben Bain Jr., free agents A'Shawn Robinson and Al-Quadin Muhammad, along with standout DT Vita Vea -- can handle business up front and Bowles can keep as many resources as possible on the backend. Bowles is particularly excited about what they have on the edge. "I feel like I don't have reserves for the first time," he said, feeling as if he can bring any one of them in on any down. -- Jenna Laine

What we're hearing on the Bengals: Sunday marks the debut of a new and improved Bengals offense. Cincinnati spent the offseason using Burrow under center more in hopes of making the offensive scheme more diverse. "I have an idea and a sense of what I want it to look and feel like over the totality of a season," OC Dan Pitcher said. "I think if we hit benchmarks that we have for ourselves internally over the long haul, it's going to pay dividends." -- Ben Baby

Stat to know: Burrow is 12-3 against NFC teams since he lost Super Bowl LVI against the Rams, which is the third-best interconference record among quarterbacks since 2022 (behind Jalen Hurts and Lamar Jackson). -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Buccaneers WR Chris Godwin Jr. will be targeted 10 or more times. Emeka Egbuka sat out time in the preseason because of a toe injury, and Mike Evans is gone. At least in the short term, I could see targets consolidating around Godwin. -- Walder

Viewers rating (out of 10): 7.7. This matchup features two teams expecting big defensive improvements facing two offenses that can pour points on when everyone is healthy. Does this still count as a QB Baker Mayfield "everyone doubted me!" campaign now that he has agreed to a big extension? Either way, I'd like to see him (and Egbuka) healthy. -- Solak

Injuries: Buccaneers | Bengals

Fantasy nugget: RB Bucky Irving is set to lead a backfield that now includes Kenny Gainwell and Sean Tucker. Even though Gainwell might cut into Irving's work as a receiver out of the backfield, Irving is still projected to lead the team in touches behind a healthy offensive line. The Bengals gave up the second-most fantasy points per game to RBs last season. See Week 1 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: The Buccaneers went 0-9 ATS in their final nine games last season. Burrow has Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, while the Bucs' defense was already struggling to get pressure without blitzing and lost Jamel Dean this offseason. That's a bad look against a QB like Burrow, who can find the open man when you send extra rushers. Cincinnati's rebuilt defense should also be better. Tampa's ATS slide could easily carry into Week 1. Read more. -- Maldonaldo

Maldonado's pick: Bengals 24, Buccaneers 17

Moody's pick: Bengals 26, Buccaneers 19

Walder's pick: Buccaneers 27, Bengals 23

FPI prediction: CIN, 60.1% (by an average of 3.1 points)

Matchup must-reads: What extending QB Mayfield means for the Bucs ... QB Burrow in it for 'long haul' with Bengals ... RB Brown won't be overlooked in Bengals' offense

Saints at Lions
1 p.m. ET | Fox | DET -7 (50.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Saints: QB Tyler Shough knows the stakes have been raised in his second season, especially now that he has been named a captain. It'll be especially important for Shough and the Saints to get off to a fast start with their first two games on the road. But Shough said the new expectations don't faze him. "There's so many different things that can happen and so many different things in the offseason that have happened. ... Expectations are going to change, but we have high expectations for ourselves." -- Katherine Terrell

What we're hearing on the Lions: All-Pro lineman Penei Sewell has fully transitioned from right to left tackle this offseason, which he says he's comfortable with entering Week 1. "Oh yeah, it's time to go now," Sewell told ESPN. Lions QB Jared Goff hasn't noticed a difference in Sewell's production on the opposite side, which he hasn't played on a full-time basis since college at Oregon (2018-19). "I think we take it for extreme granted that he was able to go over there and nothing really changed. I think he loves it," Goff said of Sewell. "Left is the premier position in football, and I think he loves that pressure and loves being the guy at the point of attack in a lot of ways." -- Eric Woodyard

Stat to know: The Saints have lost six straight games in the month of September, which is the longest active streak in the NFL and fourth-longest streak in franchise history (longest since a nine-game streak from 2014 to 2017). -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: The Lions' defense will score a touchdown. The Saints ranked 29th in pass block win rate last season, and Shough ranked 27th in sack-to-pressure ratio. Add in that the Lions are strong favorites, and I think that screams strip-sack-returned-for-a-touchdown. -- Walder

Viewers rating (out of 10): 7.1. This is a good early test for the Saints, who had one of the best defenses down the stretch of last season. The Lions should be highly explosive on offense again, especially now that RB Jahmyr Gibbs is uncontested in the backfield. -- Solak

Injuries: Saints | Lions

Fantasy nugget: Goff has averaged 19.4 fantasy points per game indoors since arriving in Detroit. This matchup also has shootout potential when you look at the total, and the Saints allowed nine quarterbacks to throw multiple touchdown passes against them last season. See Week 1 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: The Lions are 14-4 ATS in September under coach Dan Campbell. The Saints improved, but Shough's late-season surge in 2025 came against weaker defenses. Now he gets a healthier Detroit defense on the road, while the Lions' loaded offense should put immediate pressure on New Orleans to keep pace. Read more. -- Maldonaldo

Maldonado's pick: Lions 31, Saints 17

Moody's pick: Lions 33, Saints 20

Walder's pick: Lions 27, Saints 13

FPI prediction: DET, 73% (by an average of 6.7 points)

Matchup must-reads: DE Jordan (hamstring) to miss opener vs. Lions ... Respectful Lions eager to tangle with Saints in opener ... Fantasy outlook for Saints? Etienne, Johnson and rookie WRs

Bears at Panthers
1 p.m. ET | Fox | CHI -3 (46.5 O/U)

What we're hearing on the Bears: Braxton Jones was named the starting left tackle for Chicago's opener, his fifth straight Week 1 start. That's an accomplishment Jones is particularly proud of, given his path as a fifth-round pick along with how he bounced back from a knee injury in camp. Coaches said Jones grabbed hold of the position during their joint practice with Tennessee, but that doesn't mean Theo Benedet won't get playing time. "It's a real strong possibility," OL coach Dan Roushar said. "We have a lot of confidence. Both of those guys have started in Week 1 games and we've won games with them as starters. We have a lot of confidence in their ability to get the job done." -- Courtney Cronin

What we're hearing on the Panthers: The Panthers expect to use rookie nose tackle Lee Hunter in a prominent role. The rookie was named the starter between veterans Derrick Brown and Bobby Brown III on the unofficial depth chart Tuesday. When asked about the starting job Wednesday in the locker room, Hunter -- who says he is avoiding social media -- was unaware of his spot on the depth chart, saying he didn't know the team released one. Coach Dave Canales said Hunter's placement within the trenches is partially based on his summer performance but also out of "necessity" with Tershawn Wharton (neck) on the physically unable to perform list. -- Mike Kaye

Stat to know: The Panthers have lost four straight season openers, which is the second-longest active streak in the NFL, behind Tennessee's five. -- ESPN Research

Bold prediction: Bears WR Kalif Raymond will record at least four receptions. Rome Odunze (calf) is banged up. Luther Burden III (groin) sat out a lot of camp. Do you know who is a wily veteran who can be available for some layups underneath? Raymond. -- Walder

Viewers rating (out of 10): 7.2. The Bears were must-watch television last season, but the Panthers are a fairly sleepy opponent with which to open the 2026 season. If and when RB Jonathon Brooks (general soreness) makes his return from injury, the Panthers will get a watchability boost. -- Solak

Injuries: Bears | Panthers

Fantasy nugget: Tetairoa McMillan faces a Bears defense that gave up the third-most fantasy points per game to WRs and the third-most touchdowns. Chicago gave up nearly three more fantasy points than usual to opposing No. 1 receivers last season. See Week 1 rankings. -- Moody

Betting insight: The Bears have been road favorites only once since 2022 (-2.5 at the Bengals last season), but there are reasons to like them in Carolina. The Panthers' improvement last season came with a favorable schedule and a lot of close-game success. Now QB Bryce Young goes from facing one of the easiest pass-defense schedules to the second-hardest, including this Chicago team that excelled at takeaways in 2025. Read more. -- Maldonaldo

Maldonado's pick: Bears 27, Panthers 17

Moody's pick: Bears 24, Panthers 21

Walder's pick: Bears 21, Panthers 20

FPI prediction: CHI, 60.2% (by an average of 2.8 points)

stories.headline: NBA intel: How next week's BOG meeting could reshape the NBA
stories.summary: The next steps in the Clippers investigation, league expansion and NBA Europe could all be decided next week.
stories.body:
Adam Silver, now in his 12th year as NBA commissioner, has dealt with plenty of changes and challenges during his tenure. But Monday's board of governors meeting in New York represents an inflection point for the league. And his leadership will play a major role.

There are a few main agenda items that could set major events into motion that, in some cases, have been years in the making.

Most of the work by Silver and the league office has been done in the months leading up to this meeting, where the presentations and formal votes might happen, but the public rollout is a big responsibility for the commissioner, who will deliver his news conference Tuesday.

This BOG meeting has the potential to be one of more consequential ones in recent memory. Here are three topics I'm expecting Silver and the owners to discuss: the LA Clippers' investigation and punishments, NBA Europe and the next steps in expansion.

Official statements on the Clippers' salary cap circumvention punishment
Silver spoke loudly with his actions last week, slapping the Clippers with five revoked first-round draft picks and a record $30 million fine. But how he responds in front of cameras for the first time next week will set the tone going forward as this situation probably has another chapter or two to come.
The Clippers have not publicly accepted their fate or announced whether they will pursue legal action. They have not said who will act as the governor at the meeting in suspended owner Steve Ballmer's place or who will act as interim head of basketball operations in place of the suspended Lawrence Frank.

They also have not executed the trade to send Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors, a deal agreed to on the first day of free agency.

This purposeful inaction, in addition to the legal saber-rattling, can be seen as the Clippers leaving open their options and negotiation windows.

When the NBA issued its enormous penalty -- the final revoked draft pick in 2034 -- it did so knowing Ballmer might have a litigious reaction. Whether it would admit it, the league has also given itself room to negotiate. (The league and the Clippers reportedly had failed settlement discussions before the Wachtell, Lipton report was made public. )

One topic rival front offices have discussed is the less-talked-about but draconian-sounding "compliance and monitoring program by the league office for a period of five years" penalty that was also leveled on the Clippers. The terms were nebulous, probably for a reason, and the devil will surely be in the details.

"Are they going to be reading all their emails, reading their texts, listening to their phone calls?" one general manager told ESPN. "I have no idea what that [penalty] means."

The announcement of the penalty and the side deal the league cut with the players' union to have Leonard accept a $700,000 reimbursement penalty and eliminate the Clippers' option to take the NBA to arbitration, certainly changed the dynamic.

During the investigation, which spanned five major Silver news conferences, he repeatedly gave no indication of the severity of the findings, even though he said he was getting regular updates.

In the past two, before Game 1 of the 2026 Finals and after the July owners meeting in Las Vegas, Silver gave off some Judge Judy meme vibes by figuratively tapping his watch and saying the investigation needed to wrap up. It was not the posture of someone about to release a bombshell. And the Clippers, based on their public and private statements claiming shock, certainly didn't see it coming.

David Stern, Silver's legendary predecessor, was known for fiery news conferences when announcing major disciplinary actions, whether it was after the 2004 Malice at the Palace in Detroit or when he levied his own five-pick penalty to the Minnesota Timberwolves for salary cap violations in 2000. Silver is typically much more measured and disarming. When he suspended former Phoenix Suns owner Robert Sarver three years ago, Silver was even-tempered.

Soon after the report was released and the punishments announced, the Clippers issued an emotional statement and sent a seething letter to Silver. Here comes the next round.

The latest on NBA Europe -- with a possible international showdown looming
For much of the past two years, the league has been planning a major push into Europe. And recent reports have set the stage for a drama.

The Euroleague, which would be NBA Europe's main rival, is waiting for a formal offer of a partnership in the very near future and has scheduled a rare owners meeting for Oct. 5 near Lake Como in northern Italy, where it all could come to a head.

The NBA has gone through several rounds of bids and is ready to move forward with a 16-team league with 12 permanent members and four rotating members, starting in 2027. League officials have said there are bidding groups for 12 of those new teams in Europe, with franchises in London and Paris expected to go for $1 billion-plus, per league sources.

But the NBA's preference would be to blend existing Euroleague teams and new franchises into one pan-European league with NBA branding and leadership, Euroleague history and infrastructure, plus the international organization of FIBA.

That sounds nice, of course, but there's so much money and power at stake that the process to do so will be bumpy, at best.

Top officials from both the NBA and the Euroleague have said they are prepared to work together or go it alone in what surely would be an unsustainable fragmented system. It could be a seminal showdown and will be a major part of this owners meeting, multiple sources said.

The next step in NBA (domestic) expansion
The meeting could feature a vote -- or perhaps the scheduling of a vote -- to move forward with expansion, which has been long assumed but never formalized. Silver, who has said the league has been working with bankers on vetting ownership groups, could establish an exact timetable for choosing winning bids or announcing finalists.
It should not be assumed that both Las Vegas and Seattle will be on the same schedule or be close to the same price point, ownership sources said. Preliminary bidders in the $8 billion range for Vegas quickly learned the number would be higher, sources said. A Seattle team, meanwhile, could be sold for considerably less.

Some teams have been projecting the per-team payout for expansion to be $500 million to $600 million, which would put the combined expansion fee at around $15 billion to $18 billion.

Within a few months, the Los Angeles Lakers sale could close for $12.5 billion; expansion could generate a once-in-a-generation windfall for teams while also increasing their valuations; and NBA Europe might generate billions more.

With the future of those nine-, 10- and 11-figure sums potentially at stake, it's difficult to understate the importance of next week's BOG meeting for Silver and the NBA.

stories.headline: Harry Kane joins Cristiano Ronaldo in elite Champions League scoring club
stories.summary: Harry Kane joined an elite goalscoring club on Thursday after extending his remarkable Champions League streak.
stories.body:
Harry Kane joined an elite goalscoring club on Thursday after extending his remarkable Champions League streak.

Kane scored Bayern Munich's second goal in their 5-0 rout of Bodo/Glimt, meaning he has now scored in eight consecutive Champions League games.

The only players to achieve as long as a streak in the competition are Cristiano Ronaldo, Robert Lewandowski and Ruud van Nistelrooy.

Ronaldo holds the record with goals in 11 consecutive matches in 2017-18, while he also scored in eight straight for Real Madrid in 2013-14. Lewandowski also had two streaks -- of nine -- for Bayern Munich while Van Nistelrooy scored in nine straight for Manchester United in 2002-03.

Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies also netted on Thursday before a late double from Michael Olise helped Bayern kick off their Champions League campaign in style.

Kane scored 71 goals in 61 games for club and country last year and is the bookies' favourite to become England's first Ballon d'Or winner since Michael Owen at the ceremony in London next month.

- Bayern's Olise, Díaz back Kane in Ballon d'Or bid

- Musiala nets milestone Bayern Munich goal weeks after seizures

Kane has been nominated alongside the likes of Kylian Mbappé, Lamine Yamal and Lionel Messi.

"I'm proud to be nominated with my teammates," Kane said after the game.

"We won all three titles in Germany and fell just short in the Champions League. But it's out of my hands and down to the voters. It was a special season personally, but all I can do is focus on this season now."

Information from ESPN Global Research was used in this report.
